subject: Geo SLA boundary & warm-standby plan
messages:
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@northbridgebank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: operations <ops@northbridgebank.com>, Northbridge Bank Legal <legal@northbridgebank.com>
Date: 2028-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial ask — geo coverage & expected recovery windows

Kim,

Thanks for the call yesterday. To prepare for our security and procurement review, we need written confirmation of the following for public-facing inference endpoints used by Northbridge:

- RTO and RPO expectations for primary-region outage and region failover (both warm-standby and active-active scenarios).
- What parts of the stack will remain stateful across the failover (KV caches, session affinity) and what that implies for recovery time.
- Whether Redwood can accept a carve on 99.99% availability for cross-region failover window, and if so, what contractual credits accompany that.

We attached the internal audit template — please return with your proposed wording, and highlight any telemetry or runbook dependencies that affect RTO.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Cloud Ops, Northbridge Bank
[Attachment: audit_template.xlsx]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — geo coverage & expected recovery windows

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and we'll follow with a redline for your audit template by EOD tomorrow. Short answers:

- Nominal RTO (warm-standby): 10–30 minutes to restore traffic routing + 2–6 minutes for steady-state token latency depending on cache warmup.
- Nominal RTO (cold failover / rebuild): 2–4 hours; we recommend warm-standby for bank SLAs.
- RPO: customer data stored in request logs is retained per your retention policy; model-state KV caches are ephemeral — RPO is effectively last successful write (near-zero for persistent data, N/A for in-memory caches).

Important operational notes: our prefix/KV cache warming materially reduces per-token latency after failover; warm-standby with periodic KV pre-warming reduces RTO tail risks. We'll include a runbook section that details how long prefix warming takes for your typical session footprint.

I’ll loop Marcus and Aditya to prepare the redline and a proposed credits table.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-10T08:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — geo coverage & expected recovery windows

Team — drafting the technical addendum. Key items I'll propose for the NB draft (high level):

- Failover types defined: 
  * Route-only failover (no state transfer): RTO target 10–20m; degraded latency expected for first 5–30m until prefix caching reaches steady-state.
  * Warm-standby (active but idle nodes): RTO 5–15m; KV cache rehydration window 2–10m depending on footprint.
  * Rebuild from snapshot (cold): RTO 2–6h.
- RPO: Persistent logs and customer-owned stores are authoritative; for ephemeral caches RPO is best-effort (documented).
- Fallback options: If primary model instances are constrained we can route to a quantized-compatible variant with higher per-token latency but preserved semantics — suggested as an emergency mode in the SLA.
- Credits: propose a scaled credit table tied to incident classification and the declared failover type.

I’ll attach a warm-standby runbook and a sample incident timeline. Marcus
[Attachment: warm-standby-runbook.xlsx]

From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@northbridgebank.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Northbridge Bank Legal <legal@northbridgebank.com>, ops@northbridgebank.com
Date: 2028-11-10T10:11:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — geo coverage & expected recovery windows

Marcus,

This is helpful. A few follow-ups from our risk team:

- Can you quantify the cache warmup time for a 20k-user daily active footprint (estimate requests per second attached)? We need numbers to feed the risk model.
- For the ‘quantized-compatible’ emergency mode — confirm if semantics are guaranteed (same return distribution) or if we should treat it as a degraded-quality mode for read-only analytics.
- Legal asks for the exact credit % for a failover scenario where warm-standby was not deployed vs when it was.

Please put those into the redline document; we will accept a single page operational appendix that we can reference in our master services schedule.

Thanks,
Sam

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-11T13:44:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed wording + numbers for NB operational appendix

Sam — attached is a draft appendix and a short table of empirical warmup numbers based on a 20k DAU profile and the models you plan to use. Key excerpts:

- Warm-standby RTO (target): 8–12 minutes (95th percentile) including DNS and routing propagation.
- Cache rehydration: median 3 minutes, 95th percentile 9 minutes for the 20k DAU workload with our continuous prefix prefetching enabled.
- Emergency quantized fallback: semantic parity is not guaranteed; we categorize this as "degraded operational mode" and limit it to non-prod or read-only analytic workloads unless the customer signs an opt-in production fallback addendum.
- Credit table: 0.5% of monthly fee for incidents where warm-standby was active but RTO exceeded SLO; 1.5% where warm-standby was not implemented by the customer and a cross-region outage occurred.

Notes: these numbers assume the customer enables continuous KV replication for persistent artifacts and allows the Redwood agent to perform periodic pre-warms. If NB declines pre-warming, the RTO moves toward the higher end of our cold-rebuild window.

Attachments: NB_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf; timeline_and_credits.tsv

—Aditya

From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@northbridgebank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Northbridge Bank Legal <legal@northbridgebank.com>, ops@northbridgebank.com
Date: 2028-11-12T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed wording + numbers for NB operational appendix

Aditya — this is exactly the kind of specificity our auditors needed. A couple of final clarifications before I route to procurement/legal:

1) Confirm whether the 0.5% credit applies per incident or is capped monthly.
2) Where you reference "continuous KV replication" — please add a short line in the appendix describing the minimum configuration and any additional egress/ingress costs we should expect.
3) Please mark the quantized fallback as opt-in in the SLA body; legal will not accept implicit fallbacks for production inference.

If you can incorporate those tweaks, I think we can move to an internal sign-off next week and circulate a DocuSign for the SOW + operational appendix.

Thanks — Sam

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@northbridgebank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-12T18:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed wording + numbers for NB operational appendix

Sam — quick confirm:

- Credits: cap 3% monthly, applied per-incident until cap is reached. I’ll add the exact clause in the redline.
- Continuous KV replication: we’ll add the minimal configuration (replication interval, retention, and expected egress) and note that any extra cross-region storage/transfer will be billed separately at standard rates.
- Quantized fallback: will be opt-in and only available under a signed fallback addendum.

We’ll update NB_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf with these bullets and send for DocuSign link prep. Thanks for moving quickly — look forward to closing this.

—Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: NB_SLA_Draft_v3.pdf]
